overview: FAM6401 is a sim event focused on pel and emergency memory review. The notes below are organized off the canonical syllabus items first, then filled out with local FAM gouge so students can brief the event, explain the why behind each item, and stay ahead of instructor follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: a profile to safely land at a paved field with indications of engine failure. Prioritize quick setup at High Key using power while available
simulated engine failure in the landing pattern
Turn, Climb, Clean, Check, BIP, Determine, Deliver, Reduce, Lower, Report
Clean configuration (gear, flaps, speed brake up)
Another point in the ELP with proper configuration and airspeed
simulated engine failure in the landing pattern
The PEL flow remains Turn, Climb or Accelerate, Clean, Check, BIP, Determine, Deliver, Reduce, Lower, and Report.
Boost pump and Ignition - as required (ON unless airstart not warranted)
Climb or accelerate to intercept DEGA (140 KIAS climb or increase airspeed if unable to climb)
Execute PEL at or above 400’ AGL
2. CLIMB OR ACCELERATE TO INTERCEPT ELP
High Key around 3000 feet AGL with gear down and 120 KIAS.
Low Key around 1500 feet AGL with takeoff flaps and about 2/3 wingtip distance.
Review the associated WARNINGs, CAUTIONs, and NOTEs for PEL Profile and Procedures before the event.
Treat this as a cumulative emergency-procedure review. You may be assigned any previously introduced FAM EP and must know the recognition cues cold.

Know when the problem can be managed with a PEL, when it requires a forced landing, and when it is time to stop troubleshooting and eject.
If the assigned EP includes branches, know what cue drives each branch before you brief the next step.
Be ready to state the associated WARNINGs, CAUTIONs, and NOTEs for the assigned EP, not just the memory items.
